recipes.name: Dodo (Nigerian Fried Plantains)
recipes.description: Ripe plantain slices turn golden at the edges and stay soft in the middle. Serve hot alongside rice or beans.

ingredients.name: Diamond Crystal kosher salt
ingredients.prep_note: use half the volume for fine table salt

ingredients.name: neutral vegetable oil
ingredients.prep_note: for the frying pot; keep the oil depth constant when scaling servings

steps.title: Cut the plantains
steps.instruction: Trim and peel the fruit. Slice across the diagonal into pieces about 8 mm thick so the centres cook at the same rate.

steps.title: Season and heat the oil
steps.instruction: Toss the slices with the salt. Heat the oil to 175°C in a deep, heavy pan. Work in batches so the slices have room to move.

steps.title: Fry until caramelised
steps.instruction: Lower one batch into the oil. Turn the pieces as they cook. Begin checking at 8 minutes and lift out when both faces are golden and the centres are tender.
steps.timer_label: Check the colour of the first batch

steps.title: Drain and serve
steps.instruction: Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on a lined tray. Bring the oil back to temperature before frying the next batch. Serve warm.

sources.title: Ozoz Sokoh, Serious Eats: Dodo (Nigerian Plantains)
supports: yield, timing, salt ratio, 175°C frying method

sources.title: Flo Chinyere, All Nigerian Recipes: Fried Plantain or Dodo
supports: ripe firm plantains, salt and oil, batch frying and draining

recipes.review_summary: Uses Sokoh’s four side servings at the upper end of her two-to-four serving range. Her frying vessel uses 1.9 litres of oil. Oil depth depends on the pan and does not scale with servings.

recipes.name: Nigerian Chin Chin
recipes.description: Small nutmeg-scented pieces of fried dough crisp as they cool. This version uses milk, egg and melted butter.

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.prep_note: starting amount; add up to one-fifth extra if needed

ingredients.name: neutral vegetable oil
ingredients.prep_note: for frying in batches; use enough for the pan

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.instruction: Stir the flour, sugar, baking powder, nutmeg and salt together, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Bring the dough together
steps.instruction: Mix in the egg, melted butter and the initial milk. If dry flour remains, add the reserved extra milk little by little. Knead for 2–4 minutes until the dough holds together.
steps.timer_label: Check the dough after two minutes

steps.title: Cut small pieces
steps.instruction: Roll the dough out about 4–6 mm thick. Cut into strips and then crosswise into small squares. Loosen the pieces before frying.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a deep pan. Test one piece; it should bubble as it fries. Add a small batch and turn the pieces for even colour. Lift out when golden.

steps.title: Cool until crisp
steps.instruction: Drain the pieces on a lined tray. Let cool completely before serving or packing so trapped steam does not soften the crust.

sources.title: Lola Osinkolu, Chef Lola’s Kitchen: African Chin Chin
supports: eight servings, ingredient proportions, timings, kneading, rolling and frying

sources.title: Flo Chinyere, All Nigerian Recipes: Easiest Nigerian Chin Chin Recipe
supports: Nigerian snack and cutting/frying context; not the ingredient formula

recipes.review_summary: Uses the Chef Lola version with nutmeg. The original milk range is 5–6 tablespoons for eight; the scalable ingredient gives its lower end and permits up to 20% extra.
